LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Production.About.Title: About this page
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Production.About.Body:
Console orders live here: the full list is on the left, and the selected order is shown on the right. An order describes what to make and how much, including the product, materials, workbenches, and workers.
The console does not force colonists to work. It places normal RimWorld bills on workbenches, and colonists take them according to their work priorities and schedule. If an order is ready but its worker is asleep or fighting a fire, the console is not holding it up.
Changes made on the order card reach the workbenches during the next update, usually a little over a second later.
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Production.List.Title: Order list
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Production.What.Title: What to make
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Production.Who.Title: Who does the work
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Production.Who.Body:
Leave Anyone enabled to let any suitable colonist take the job. Select workers by name when you want the order restricted to those colonists, even if somebody else is available nearby.
Selected workers who cannot do the job are marked in red. Their required work type may be disabled on the Work tab, their skill may be too low, or they may be incapable of that work. The console warns you but does not change those settings, since work restrictions are usually intentional.
The Use checkbox on the Colonists page takes priority. A colonist disabled there will never be assigned to a console order.
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Production.From.Title: Materials and sources
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Production.Where.Title: Workbenches and destination
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Production.Stats.Title: Statistics
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Production.Stats.Body:
The Made line shows three values: how much this order has produced, how much was requested, and how many of that item are currently in storage.
The last value drives Maintain stock mode. If the amount in storage increases through trade, loot, or another mod, the console notices and stops producing until more is needed.
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Wizard.About.Title: How the wizard works
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Wizard.About.Body:
The wizard builds an order one step at a time: product, amount, material sources, allowed materials, workbenches, workers, destination, and summary.
Next remains disabled until the current step is complete. This prevents half-configured orders, such as one with no workbench capable of completing it.
You can go back at any time without losing your choices. Nothing in the game changes until you confirm the order on the final step.
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Wizard.Product.Title: Product
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Wizard.Product.Body:
The list is built from the game's own data, so recipes and workbenches added by other mods appear automatically.
Each product shows whether it can be made right now: whether a suitable bench exists, the research is complete, and the materials are available. Products shown in red cannot be selected, preventing an order that is blocked from the moment it is created.
Use the categories on the left to narrow the list, or search by product name.
A product with a larger-output recipe appears on two rows: “Simple meal” uses any recipe, while “Simple meal ×4” uses only the four-meal recipe.
You can tick several products at once to create a batch of orders.
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Wizard.Quantity.Title: Amount
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Wizard.Quantity.Body:
The three modes answer different questions:
— fixed amount: "make 50 chairs, then stop"; — maintain stock: "always keep 50 meals in storage"; — forever: "keep making this until I say stop."
Operations without a product, such as butchering or smelting, are measured in recipe runs instead of items.
If a recipe makes more than one item per run, a fixed amount counts whole runs: 50 with the ×4 recipe becomes 52, and the field shows how many runs that is.
Maintain stock counts items in storage plus items colonists are carrying. Items lying on the floor count once they are hauled to storage.
The initial values come from the console settings. If your usual order is two hundred items, you do not need to replace the default ten every time.
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Wizard.Sources.Title: Material sources
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Wizard.Ingredients.Body:
Choose which materials the order may use. By default, everything accepted by the recipe is allowed.
Clear an option when you need to reserve that material for something else. For example, forbid wood so colonists burn chemfuel and leave the logs for construction.
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Wizard.Benches.Title: Workbenches
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Wizard.Benches.Body:
You select individual workbenches on the map, not just a workbench type. This lets an order use one workshop without touching another.
A bench reserved by another console order cannot be selected. The card shows which order is using it, and it becomes available once that order is completed or stopped.
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Wizard.Executors.Title: Workers
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Wizard.Executors.Body:
Anyone leaves the job open to every suitable colonist, so the order will not stall just because one named worker falls ill.
If you select workers by name, check the notes beside them. A colonist with the required work type disabled or insufficient skill remains visible, but will not perform the job.
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Wizard.StoreTo.Title: Destination
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Wizard.StoreTo.Body:
Any suitable storage uses normal RimWorld behavior: the crafter hauls finished goods according to your storage settings.
Choose a specific storage when the product is needed in one place, such as medicine in the hospital or components beside a workbench. If that storage fills up, the console will show it as the reason the order stopped.
Drop on floor: the crafter drops the result next to the workbench and starts the next item right away, while other colonists haul it to storage. Useful when you have one crafter and enough haulers.
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Wizard.Summary.Title: Summary
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Wizard.Summary.Body:
The final step shows the entire order: what to make, how much, who may work, which materials and workbenches may be used, and where the result goes. This is your last chance to adjust it before creation.
After confirmation, the order appears on the Production page and starts running. Every choice can still be edited on its order card, so you do not need to repeat the wizard.
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Animals.About.Title: About this page
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Animals.About.Body:
The species list is on the left, and the selected species is shown on the right. Settings apply to the species as a whole—"manage every alpaca this way"—rather than to one animal at a time.
The console uses the same Tame, Slaughter, and Hunt designations you can place manually. Colonists carry them out according to their work priorities. If nobody has Handle enabled on the Work tab, the designations will simply remain unfinished.
If you are not interested in a species, leave it alone. The console will not touch it until automation is enabled.
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Animals.Auto.Title: Automation
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Animals.Auto.Body:
The checkbox below the species name is the main switch: either you manage the species yourself, or the console does.
When disabled, the console leaves that species completely alone. It will not tame, hunt, or slaughter it, and any designations you placed yourself remain yours.
When enabled, the three sections below become active, each with its own checkbox. The designation columns in the animal tables are then locked because the console is managing those same designations and would otherwise undo your manual changes on its next update.
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Animals.Limits.Title: Population limits
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Animals.Limits.Body:
One table answers two questions at once: which animals should be tamed, and which should be slaughtered. Below the minimum, the console tames more. Above the maximum, it marks extras for slaughter.
Rows represent sex; columns represent Total and the three life stages. Total is not the combined number of males and females. It is a separate limit for each sex, so a milk herd can favor females while avoiding too many males that only fight and eat.
Life-stage limits answer a different question: which animals should be affected once the limit for that sex is crossed. A group that exceeds its own maximum by the largest amount is handled first, while a group already at its minimum is never reduced. Taming mirrors this logic by favoring the group furthest below its minimum.
Each cell has its own mode: Unlimited has no restriction, Range sets a minimum and maximum, and Exact keeps precisely that number.
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Animals.Taming.Title: Taming
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Animals.Taming.Body:
The console designates wild animals of this species for taming while the tamed population remains below its limits.
Unlimited attempts to tame every eligible animal it can reach, regardless of population. Use limits follows the table.
The Animals to tame checkboxes select life stages. Babies are easier to tame, but take longer to mature.
Area and medical care are assigned as soon as an animal is tamed, saving you from updating each one manually. If a suitable pen exists, pens are offered instead of areas because colonists will take the animal there anyway.
The orange warning shows the chance that a failed tame attempt will trigger an attack. Predators are especially dangerous.
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Animals.Hunting.Title: Hunting
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Animals.Hunting.Body:
This is not a target for how many animals to kill. It is a reserve—the number that should remain on the map. Wildlife can recover naturally as long as it is not hunted to extinction, and the reserve protects against that.
Set the reserve separately by life stage and sex. Every eligible animal above it is marked for hunting.
Injured animals may attack the hunter; the warning badge shows the chance. Hunting predators often turns into a fight, so enable it deliberately.
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Animals.Slaughter.Title: Slaughter
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Animals.Slaughter.Body:
The console marks tamed animals above the limits for slaughter, a few at a time instead of designating the whole herd at once.
Priority decides which animals go first: oldest or youngest. Older animals have less life ahead of them, while younger ones still have time to grow.
Two options are disabled by default: slaughtering pregnant animals and animals bonded to a colonist. Losing offspring or causing a master's mood penalty often costs more than feeding one extra animal.
While this section is enabled, vanilla auto-slaughter is disabled for the species. Two independent rules acting on the same herd would produce results neither one intended.
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Animals.Tables.Title: Animal tables
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Animals.Tables.Body:
The bottom of the card contains two lists: tamed animals of this species and wild ones currently on the map.
The tamed list shows name, sex, age, master, and bond; pregnant animals have a green marker. Slaughter and Release place the normal RimWorld designations immediately without waiting for Save.
The wild list shows sex, age, and Tame and Hunt columns. Use these to target a specific animal without handing the entire species over to the console.
When Automation is enabled, the checkboxes remain visible but cannot be changed, preventing you and the console from fighting over the same designations.
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Growing.About.Title: About this page
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Growing.About.Body:
Fields, growing zones, and hydroponics are listed on the left, with the selected field on the right. The console chooses the crop and manages the cycle; colonists still sow and harvest normally.
A field you have not handed over to the console remains untouched, and you choose its crop yourself.
The filters on the left narrow the list by type and state: hydroponics, growing zones, managed fields, idle fields, or blighted fields.
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Growing.Sowing.Title: Sowing and modes
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Growing.Queue.Title: Crop queue
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Growing.Queue.Body:
Drag crops from Available to Queue. Queue entries can also be reordered by dragging, or removed with the cross.
The next crop is assigned only after the field is empty. The console waits for colonists to finish the harvest before changing crops so that half the field is not left unripe.
While it waits, the console closes the field with a hidden service crop. This prevents colonists from sowing the previous crop again, and the field card tells you when this is happening.
Repeat queue loops back to the beginning. Without it, the field stops after the final crop.
You can copy a field plan and paste it onto other fields instead of rebuilding the same queue for every growing zone.
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Growing.Blight.Title: Blight
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Growing.Blight.Body:
Cut blighted plants designates infected plants for cutting and prevents new sowing until the field is clear.
Stopping sowing is part of the treatment, not an extra precaution. Colonists normally cut and sow at the same time, allowing new plants to catch blight from infected neighbors and making the cleanup endless. The console temporarily closes the field with a hidden service crop, then restores the previous crop after the blight is gone.
Enabling this option gives the console partial control of the field even if normal sowing management is disabled.
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.General.About.Title: What the console does
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.General.About.Body:
The console brings colony production into one window: orders, workbenches, workers, storages, fields, and herds. Instead of visiting every workbench, you can see the full picture at a glance.
The mod does not patch RimWorld or replace its systems. It places the same bills and designations you would use manually, then keeps them coordinated for you.
The catalog is built from the game's own data, so recipes, workbenches, and animals added by other mods are detected without manual setup.
The mod runs on RimWorld 1.6 and 1.7: the same download works with both versions of the game.
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.General.Window.Title: Window layout
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.General.Window.Body:
The tabs across the top open each section. Most pages show a list on the left and the selected item's details on the right.
New order opens the wizard, the cog opens Settings, and ? opens this help window. Help starts on the page that matches the section you were viewing.
Red and yellow badges always include a written reason. The console will not warn you about a problem without explaining it.
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.General.Limits.Title: What the mod does not do
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.General.Limits.Body:
The console does not force colonists to work. Their work priorities, schedules, and moods remain under your control; the console only assigns bills and designations.
It does not remove your manual designations or compete with them. Anything you place yourself remains yours until you explicitly hand that object over to the console.
It does not create items from nothing or speed up production. When something is missing, it tells you what the problem is, but your colony must solve it through normal gameplay.
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Overview.About.Title: About this page
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Overview.About.Body:
Overview answers one question: is everything working? This page is read-only and contains no settings.
The counters at the top show how many orders are active, currently being worked on, waiting, or stopped. Workbench load shows how many benches are working, busy with something else, or unavailable.
Last update shows when the console last compared its orders with the map. If the timer keeps increasing without resetting, the game is paused.
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Overview.Attention.Body:
This table collects every order that is not moving: blocked and paused orders, together with the reason.
Click a row to open that order on the Production page, where its settings can be fixed.
Finishing soon on the right shows which products will be completed first. It is useful when you are waiting for a specific item and deciding whether to create another order.
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Overview.Stock.Title: Stock overview
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Overview.Stock.Body:
The bottom panel shows what is stored, how much current orders require, and the resulting balance.
A red required value means orders need more than the colony currently has. This is not necessarily an error—the material may already be on its way. If the value does not change for several days, however, nobody may be producing or gathering it.
The Stock overview tab provides the same information in greater detail.
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Benches.About.Title: About this page
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Benches.About.Body:
Workbench types are listed on the left, and the selected type is shown on the right. The console groups benches by type rather than listing them all separately: ten tailoring benches appear as one type with ten instances.
The Use checkbox determines whether the console may place orders on this workbench type at all. Clear it to keep those benches entirely under manual control.
Individual benches can still be excluded from the list below—for example, to reserve a remote bench for manual bills.
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Benches.Card.Title: What the card shows
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Benches.Card.Body:
General information shows how many benches of this type exist, how many are ready, and what they are doing.
Instances lists each workbench separately, including whether it is reserved by a console order, available, and currently working.
Recipes shows what this workbench can make and whether the required resources and skills are available. Use it to understand why an order was not assigned to this bench.
Output over 7 days shows how much was produced on workbenches of this type.
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Executors.About.Title: About this page
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Executors.About.Body:
This page lists colonists and autonomous machines that can participate in production, with details for the selected worker.
The Use checkbox allows the console to assign that colonist to orders. Clear it to leave them free for other work.
Ignore is a stronger option. An ignored worker is completely hidden from the console and will not appear in any selection list. Use it for guests, slaves, or anyone you do not consider part of the production workforce.
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Executors.Card.Title: What the card shows
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Executors.Card.Body:
Information shows the colonist's current state and activity.
Skills lists production-related skills and passions, helping you decide who should handle precise work.
Orders and Workbenches show where this colonist is assigned and help explain why they are busy.
Output over 7 days shows how much they produced. It is not a performance review; it helps reveal workers who are assigned on paper but never actually work.
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Storage.About.Title: About this page
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Storage.About.Body:
Stockpile zones, shelves, and storage groups are listed on the left, with the selected storage on the right.
The Use checkbox determines whether the console may take materials from this storage or send finished goods to it. Clear it to keep the storage entirely under manual control.
Storages can be renamed directly from this page. The new name is used both in RimWorld and throughout the console.
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Storage.Card.Title: What the card shows
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Storage.Card.Body:
Information shows capacity, current load, and storage filters.
Orders lists the console orders that take materials from this storage or deliver products to it. Check this list before removing a storage.
Contents shows everything currently stored and can be searched by item name.
The Stock overview tab presents the same data from the opposite direction: grouped by item rather than storage, with the balance between available and required amounts.
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Settings.About.Title: Settings
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Settings.About.Body:
Settings apply to every colony and are stored in the player's configuration file rather than in a save.
There are four sections: update intervals, autonomous workbenches, defaults for new orders, and section checkboxes.
Reset restores the original defaults.
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Settings.Timings.Title: Update intervals
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Settings.Timings.Body:
There are separate intervals for orders, growing, and animals—and they are separate for a reason.
Orders update frequently because clearing a checkbox should remove a bill from its workbench right away. Fields and herds change over hours of game time, so checking them just as often would add load without improving responsiveness.
If a large colony starts to stutter, increase the Growing and Animals intervals first. Order updates are inexpensive and usually do not need changing.
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Settings.Defaults.Title: Default values
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Settings.Defaults.Body:
Every value entered in the wizard has a starting default: fixed amount, target stock, order mode, source and destination storage modes, and the Anyone checkbox.
Each colony has its usual order size. If you normally make two hundred at a time, there is no reason to replace the default ten for every order.
The section checkboxes below control sterilization, slaughtering pregnant or bonded animals, cutting blighted plants, and cutting the current crop. They only set the initial state for a NEW species or NEW field; existing setups are not changed.

LanguageData.ProdConsole.Variant.Title: Recipe variant
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Wizard.StoreTo.FloorText: The crafter drops the result next to the workbench and starts the next item right away; other colonists haul it to storage. It counts toward stock once it has been hauled.
LanguageData.ProdConsole.Help.Production.Variant.Body:
Some products have several recipes with different output: a simple meal can be cooked one at a time or four at once.
— any suitable: each workbench uses the first recipe it knows, starting with the smallest output; — a specific variant: the order uses only that recipe, and only workbenches that know it work on the order.
When a recipe makes more than one item per run, Exact amount counts whole runs: an order for 50 meals with the ×4 recipe becomes 52, and the field shows this right away along with the number of runs. In Keep in stock mode, stock may go a few items over the target, because the last run is always finished.
